text:
alex-s: Heads up — Legal just emailed a DSAR from an EU user. They want a full account export and deletion, and explicitly asked for deletion from backups. Do we have an established retention-exception / backup-purge path for DSARs?

maria-privacy: Thanks Alex. Can you drop the customer_id and the DSAR timestamp? Also: do they claim any specific data categories (logs, embeddings, support transcripts)?

jia-support: customer_id=cu_92b4f, DSAR received 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z. They mentioned "all personal data" and referenced chat transcripts from support. I've flagged the ticket.

sam-infra: Quick summary of infra constraints: backups are incremental snapshots in our S3 bucket, lifecycle 90 days. Backups are encrypted with our platform KMS key (not customer-managed). We don't have a safe per-customer key rotation today. Purging a specific user's data from all backup deltas is non-trivial.

nina-sre: Audit logs (who-accessed-what) are stored in a separate immutable retention bucket for 365 days for compliance. We can redact user identifiers in downstream analytics but the raw logs are append-only. Legal might accept redaction for logs.

maria-privacy: Under GDPR we need to honor deletion requests unless an applicable exception applies. For backups: two tracks recommended — 1) immediate deletion from live systems and services; 2) retention-exception review for backups/audit-logs that are difficult to purge. If approved, we document the exception and a mitigations plan (e.g., limited retention, access controls, redaction).

olivia-legal-bot: Policy excerpt: "Backup deletion requests require a documented retention-exception review and signoff from Privacy + Security + Infra. See form: https://redwood.internal/retention-exceptions" :lock:

alex-s: OK — practical Qs: how do we prove deletion to the user? Audit trail? And can KMS key rotation be used as an irreversible removal tactic?

sam-infra: For proof we can provide a deletion certificate: job id, affected tables, start/end timestamps, and object manifest. Key-rotation idea: rotating the platform KMS would affect all backups/platform data — not acceptable. We could: (a) maintain a per-customer envelope key in the future; (b) for this case, identify backup objects containing the customer and remove those objects or rewrite deltas to exclude records (expensive).

jia-support: Customer-facing template needed. What can we promise now vs later? Immediate: account disabled + export delivered. Later: backup purge subject to retention-exception outcome — ETA?

maria-privacy: Proposed immediate steps (short bullets):
- Disable account and create export (jia)
- Run live-data purge job (alex + sam)
- Open retention-exception request (maria + sam) with details & mitigation
- Evaluate logs redaction (nina)
- Draft DSAR response listing what we deleted vs what remains and timelines (jia)

sam-infra: I'll investigate whether backups contain row-level deltas we can selectively rewrite. If not, fallback is targeted object deletion + metadata reconciliation. I'll also check if we have any per-customer encryption envelope metadata to leverage. ETA: 24h.

nina-sre: I'll run a quick scan to map which log indices reference cu_92b4f and create a redaction plan. If redaction is possible, we can mark those logs as redacted and include proof. ETA: 24h.

jia-support: I'll draft the DSAR reply and propose language: "We have deleted your account and provided the export. Backups and audit logs are subject to a retention-exception review; we will update you within 7 business days."

maria-privacy: I'll open the retention-exception ticket now and add legal signoff as an approver. Link it to the DSAR case.

alex-s: Action owners: sam (backup feasibility + KMS options), nina (logs mapping/redaction), jia (customer reply + export), maria (exception ticket + legal). Please update the ticket with short notes as you make progress.

jia-support: one more: support needs the exact deletion job command for runbook. Sam / Alex can you paste the snippet when ready?

sam-infra: Will post a safe runbook snippet after I confirm approach. For now here's the list command to find backups referencing the customer:```rdb-backups list --customer-id=cu_92b4f --format=json```

alex-s: fine. Let's reconvene in this thread once we have the 24h scans. Thanks all. :pray:
